name: SF6 Character Production
description: SF6-specific character creation using source evidence, explicit project deviations, connected asset/code/system workspaces, fast transactional drafts, evidence-backed QA, reusable lessons, and JNP signoff.
sourceAuthority: Street Fighter 6 behavior and research, with every intentional system or character deviation recorded explicitly.
completionModel: Source reproduction, deviation review, evidence-backed QA, reusable lesson capture, and JustNoPoint/JNP owner sign-off.
ownershipScope: SF6 game policy and character implementations. Reusable mechanisms belong to the Universal Template.
reopenTriggers: An upstream engine update changes verified behavior.
A shared mechanism or game policy used by the baseline changes.
New source evidence disproves a frozen rule.
A port uncovers an undocumented dependency or exception.

phases.name: 1. SF6 Source and Character Definition
phases.summary: Establish source identity, complete move/system inventory, controls, options, deviations, and unresolved design decisions before implementation is treated as authoritative.

steps.label: Import and review SF6 character, move, mechanic, and author-decision knowledge
Record gameplay identity, strengths, weaknesses, range, and intended project role
Inventory normals, command normals, throws, specials, Supers, system actions, and added or removed material
Record Classic/Modern routes, alternate modes, costumes, colors, variants, FX colors, and Character Options
Separate SF6 source behavior, normalized equivalents, project deviations, implemented values, and signed-off values
Map shared SF6 systems, unique helpers/projectiles/effects, and connected character files

phases.name: 2. SF6 Assets and Presentation Foundation
phases.summary: Build and validate SFF, AIR, palettes, sounds, layers, companions, effects, and presentation while keeping asset and gameplay completion separate.

steps.label: Classify, build, and validate SFF groups, indices, axes, layers, transformations, aliases, archives, and required sprites
Author AIR actions, timing, offsets, collision, push/width/depth overlays, and missing-sprite review
Configure true-color PalFX, indexed compatibility where needed, costumes, base colors, variants, and FX color ownership
Map split character, voice, common-FX, project sounds, commands, timing, and ownership
Record layers, parts, companions, projectiles, helpers, effects, and their deterministic lifecycle
Review intros, win poses, taunts, get hits, KOs, sparks, voices, effects, and UI presentation
Confirm palette, layer, axis, sprite-name, and frame results agree across SFF, AIR, move, throw, and live-game views
Classify asset groups as Placeholder, Gameplay Ready, Presentation Ready, or Final without confusing asset and behavior completion
Rebuild from saved manifests and verify groups, indices, axes, palettes, layers, and sound assignments reproduce the reviewed result

phases.name: 3. SF6 Movement, Controls, and Commands
phases.summary: Normalize and author movement trajectories, Classic/Modern commands, route priority, character options, and online-safe input ownership.

steps.label: Author and compare walking, crouching, jumping, turning, dashes, landing, and unique movement trajectories
Validate motions, charge, timing, step buffers, facing, negative edge, simultaneous buttons, and priority
Validate Classic commands, Modern shortcuts/modifiers, Special/Drive/Super routes, and collisions
Confirm enabled Character Options resolve deterministically and hide disabled or fixed Quick Select choices

phases.name: 4. SF6 Attack and System Authoring
phases.summary: Author connected attack data and integrate every applicable SF6 offense, Drive, Super, armor, collision-region, reaction, resource, and communication mechanism.

steps.label: Author startup, active, recovery, animation, movement, collision, reach, vulnerability, sparks, and sounds
Author hit/guard pause, stun, reactions, velocities, knockdown, Counter Hit, Punish Counter, and same-tick behavior
Author damage, chip, scaling, life/red life, Super, Drive, stun, score, and Modern modifiers
Author links, target combos, chains, Drive Rush, special/OD/Super, whiff, conditional, and destination-state cancels
Integrate applicable Drive Impact, Parry/Perfect Parry, Drive Rush, Drive Reversal, OD, Burnout, cooldown, gain, and spending behavior
Integrate applicable Supers/Critical Art, armor/Armor Break, recoverable life, hit regions, throws, and character exceptions
Validate projectile/helper/companion spawn, movement, clash, contact, cleanup, ownership, and presentation

phases.name: 5. SF6 Fast Drafts, QA, and Signoff Preparation
phases.summary: Optionally apply high-confidence source drafts transactionally, review exceptions in batches, run applicable behavior matrices, and preserve evidence without granting automatic completion.

steps.label: Create a character checkpoint and configure optional Auto-Apply Source Draft categories/confidence
Apply qualifying drafts while automatically preserving source, previous, formula, applied, dependency, validation, and undo records
Review ambiguous, unsupported, destructive, dependency-incomplete, and manually diverged cases
Compare, revise, accept, or revert applied moves and properties in a batch review
Run applicable whiff, hit, guard, Counter, Punish, air, corner, armor, Parry, Drive, cancel, resource, and entity tests
Record evidence, intentional deviations, accepted limitations, failures, and linked tickets
Confirm assets, behavior, systems, presentation, options, dependencies, tests, and lessons are ready for JNP signoff

phases.name: 6. Ryu Baseline v1 Freeze
phases.summary: Rehearse the complete workflow, capture what was learned, and freeze the first reusable SF6 foundation without claiming unfinished art or moves are complete.

steps.label: Freeze the source and deviation ledger
steps.acceptance: Every foundational behavior identifies SF6 source evidence, an approved project deviation, or a known limitation.

steps.label: Resolve and sign off the current SFF/AIR repair list
steps.acceptance: Known rebuild omissions, palette defaults, axes, visibility, required sprites, and required animations are corrected or ticketed.

steps.label: Run the full asset-to-signoff workflow rehearsal
steps.acceptance: The Ryu path is performed from source assets through SFF, AIR, constants, state code, sounds, live tests, logger evidence, and review; every friction point becomes a ticket.

steps.label: Capture the reusable Ryu lesson packet
steps.learning: A reusable lesson records the proven rule, game-specific exception, test procedure, evidence, known limitation, and owner sign-off.
steps.acceptance: The lesson is useful to the next implementer without silently turning Ryu-specific policy into a universal rule.

steps.label: Record Ryu Baseline v1 and owner sign-off
steps.acceptance: JustNoPoint or JNP names the frozen version, reviews evidence and limitations, and authorizes Demitri to inherit the hardened process.
